articles.title: Chiefs Rookie Emmett Johnson Scores a Touchdown in His First NFL Start Against Atlanta; How an Unexpected Opportunity Became an Early Career Milestone
articles.summary: Emmett Johnson made the most of his big break when the Kansas City Chiefs gave him his first NFL start against the Atlanta Falcons.
articles.body: Emmett Johnson made the most of his big break when the Kansas City Chiefs gave him his first NFL start against the Atlanta Falcons. After an injury opened up a spot, he stepped up and played a great game. He proved he can both run the ball and catch passes, which gave the Chiefs another dependable playmaker. Scoring two touchdowns was a huge early milestone in his pro career, and it quickly won him praise from his teammates and coaches.Emmett Johnson's Journey to the Kansas City ChiefsJohnson earned his reputation as a star back during his time at Nebraska. In 2025, he put together a huge season with 1,451 rushing yards and 12 scores, which earned him Big Ten Running Back of the Year honors and a spot on the AP All-American second team. His strong play caught the eye of NFL scouts. The Kansas City Chiefs selected him in the fifth round with the 161st overall pick in April 2026.The Opportunity That Put Him in the Starting LineupJohnson spent the start of the season waiting his turn behind established starter Kenneth Walker III. When a groin injury kept Walker out of the Week 10 game against Atlanta on November 15, 2026, Johnson finally got his shot. The Chiefs turned to their rookie, giving him his first NFL start. Although the opportunity came at short notice, Johnson had already been learning the team's offensive system and preparing for a larger role.Emmett Johnson's Breakthrough Against AtlantaJohnson wasted little time making an impact at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. During Kansas City's opening scoring drive, he caught a 12-yard touchdown pass from Patrick Mahomes in the first quarter. He later added another touchdown reception, this time on a six-yard pass in the fourth quarter. Both scores came through the air, showing that Johnson could offer more than just a running option in the Chiefs' offense.Johnson finished the game with 101 rushing yards on 22 carries and six receptions for 70 yards. His 171 total yards from scrimmage and two receiving touchdowns made him one of Kansas City's standout performers in the 35-13 victory. He also recorded 10 forced missed tackles, according to NFL Pro data cited by Sports Illustrated.Johnson's Early NFL Career MilestoneThe Atlanta game was a big step forward for Johnson because it showed how quickly he was picking up the pro game. Head coach Andy Reid praised how well-prepared the rookie was, especially for knowing the playbook, doing his blocking jobs well, and protecting the quarterback. Reid also mentioned that Johnson has clearly earned the trust of his teammates. Those qualities helped him handle the responsibility of starting when the Chiefs needed him.Johnson's performance also caught the attention of Mahomes, who praised his ability to run hard, break tackles, and make plays as a receiver. The quarterback was pleased to see the rookie take advantage of an opportunity that had arrived with little notice.What Lies Ahead for Emmett Johnson? His Potential Role in the Chiefs' OffenseJohnson’s strong game against Atlanta gave Kansas City another weapon in its running back rotation. Even though the Chiefs expected Kenneth Walker III back for their next game against the Arizona Cardinals, having both backs ready gives Andy Reid’s offense a nice boost, especially with Johnson's pass-catching skills and depth.For Johnson, the challenge will be to maintain the same preparation and consistency as the season progresses. His first start showed that he could handle a bigger workload, but he will need to keep earning opportunities through his outstanding performances. The Atlanta game gave the rookie a strong foundation to build on as he continues his NFL journey.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Josh Allen vs. Patrick Mahomes: Why Thanksgiving night in Buffalo is the NFL season's biggest quarterback showdown
articles.summary: Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes meet Thursday night in Buffalo, and the numbers between them point in two directions.
articles.body: Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes meet Thursday night in Buffalo, and the numbers between them point in two directions. Allen is 5-1 against Mahomes in the regular season. Mahomes is 4-0 against Allen in the playoffs. Kickoff is 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock, and it will be the first Thanksgiving game the Bills have ever hosted. Buffalo leads the AFC and Kansas City arrives off three straight blowouts. Ten meetings since 2020 have produced an even split. Neither side wants to hand the other a win on a stage this big.Why Thanksgiving night in Buffalo is the season's biggest quarterback showdownNo other quarterback matchup this season carries this much weight. The Chiefs and Bills have played ten times since 2020, and each side has five wins. That sounds tidy. It is not. Allen has won five of the six regular season meetings. Mahomes has won all four in the playoffs.NBC has branded it the rivalry of the decade, and for once the billing does not feel like marketing. The game closes a Thanksgiving tripleheader that begins with Bears at Lions and Eagles at Cowboys. The broadcast starts at 7 p.m. ET on NBC, with streaming on Peacock.Allen's most recent win over Kansas City was a statement. He threw for 273 yards and accounted for three touchdowns, and Buffalo's defense kept Mahomes under pressure before stopping a late Kansas City drive that could have tied it.Mahomes has the other side of it. His last playoff win over Allen came in the 2025 AFC Championship Game, and he has never lost to him in the postseason.Pressure is the detail to watch. Buffalo bothered Mahomes in their last meeting. If it happens again, Kansas City will need Reid to find answers quickly.Then there is the holiday itself. Allen is 3-0 on Thanksgiving, with wins over Dallas, New Orleans and Detroit. None of those teams had Mahomes. Buffalo is 6-4-1 on the day overall but has never hosted one before. Travis Kelce already has a read on it. "Obviously, Pat Mahomes and Josh Allen is always an instant classic," the Chiefs tight end said.How the Chiefs and Bills arriveLast season hurt both teams, just in different ways. Kansas City went 6-11 and missed the playoffs, a rare miss for a franchise that had become a January regular. Buffalo went 12-5 and lost a heartbreaker to Denver in the divisional round.The Chiefs have found a rhythm. They led Arizona 34-7 in the fourth quarter Sunday, and Andy Reid sent Justin Fields in for Mahomes rather than risk an injury in a game that was over. It was their third blowout in a row.The prep window is short. Sunday's game left Kansas City with four days to get ready for Allen.Kansas City still has Travis Kelce and Xavier Worthy as targets for Mahomes. Buffalo has running back James Cook and receiver Khalil Shakir around Allen. Both offenses have options. Whoever's quarterback gets more time will probably decide it.Early lines made the Bills a three-point favorite, so Kansas City is the underdog on the road.Thursday is a regular season game, and that column has leaned Allen's way five to one. If Mahomes wants to change the pattern, Buffalo gives him a national stage to do it.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
